opening_message:
Ticket 1: Dominic Taylor (employee ID E004) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E004.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Dominic Taylor (E004) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code, owned by the Engineer role. Full-time employees may have up to write, and the role owns the system, so write is within policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E004 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, maximum is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The team notes conflict on employment type: HR note lists E004 as full-time Engineer (recommending write), while the Security note states the Security DB shows E004 is a contractor with basic security training (recommending read). Policy for contractors allows read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps access at read. Because the requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, and the security record is the more authoritative source for contractor status, I grant the maximum permitted level: read.
